title: The Yellow Line Still Means It
scene: Clear cold afternoon. A Kent school zone with a solid yellow in your lane and a broken yellow for them. You want around a parked delivery van that has been dead since the first week. The van sits legal enough. Passing would put you over the solid. The playground is empty. The line is not. Hollis is not in this one. Nobody is coming the other way that you can see. That is the whole trick of a solid yellow: the thing you cannot see yet owns that paint.
decision: A dead van is blocking your speed and the yellow under you is solid. Do you go around?

options.text: Stay behind the van until you can pass where the yellow breaks, even if that is slow
options.result: You wait. A block later the yellow breaks. You check, pass, and recover before the next solid. A car you did not have comes the other way in the gap you would have occupied. The van keeps being dead. You keep being in your lane.

options.text: Go around now — nothing is coming and the van is the real hazard
options.result: You cross the solid. The other car was in the school-zone dip. Two plows of width, one lane, a freeze. You dive back and scrape the van. Paint on primer. The yellow was not decorative.

options.text: Straddle the yellow to peek, then decide
options.result: You are already in their lane to peek. Peeking is occupying. The dip car has to take the curb. You learned the sightline by stealing it.

options.text: Use the parking lane on the right to sneak past without crossing yellow
options.result: The parking lane is a door zone of ghosts. A van door that was not quite latched opens into your mesh. You pass the delivery van and inherit a different one. Right was not free. It was unsearched.

debrief: A solid yellow on your side means do not pass. Empty and legal are not the same. Wait for the broken yellow and a sightline. The parked van is a delay. The solid line is a rule.

source.psdp_skill: Skill five: driving on a quiet street – part one
source.teaching_target: Do not pass on a solid yellow line on your side; wait for a broken line and adequate sight distance.

image_brief.subject: oblique overhead: faded matte-pink VW Beetle queued behind a dead primer van, both facing away, plow at the van's rear toward top of frame
image_brief.foreground: school-zone pavement, a faded painted 20, wet or cold-dry asphalt
image_brief.midground: two parallel yellows: SOLID and continuous nearer her for the full frame; BROKEN dashes with clear gaps on the far side — that difference is the focus
image_brief.background: empty playground fence, clear cold afternoon, long blue shadows, no oncoming visible yet
image_brief.read: the only legal pass is where the yellow breaks — solid yellow on this side, not here
